title: Deployment Gatekeeper: Vetting checklist and RBAC for model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and deliver a gated approval workflow (console + API) for production model rollouts that enforces role-based approvals, captures auditable decision records, and integrates with canary/A-B/shadow traffic controls and auto-rollback policies.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC: Console and API enforce three configurable roles for rollout approvals (requester, approver, emergency-approver) with mapping to SSO groups and service accounts.
Approval workflow: Teams can create rollout requests with required sign-off list; rollout cannot progress to canary or full traffic without recorded approvals.
Audit trail: Every approval/rejection/override is recorded in an append-only audit log with timestamp, actor, reason, and linked rollout snapshot; exportable as CSV/JSON for 12 months retention.
Canary/A-B integration: Approval gates are pluggable into canary and A/B flows so that traffic promotion requires explicit acceptance unless auto-approve policy is set for low-risk model variants.

Auto-rollback hooks: Console allows configuration of rollback triggers (latency p90, error rate, quality regression by eval set). Rollback events must generate an incident ticket link and appear in audit logs.
API parity: All console actions are available through the Redwood API with the same permission checks and audit metadata.
E2E tests: Automated tests simulate approval, rejection, override, and auto-rollback; CI asserts audit log entries and that traffic never exceeds configured thresholds without approvals.
Documentation: Public runbook and internal playbook describing when to require multi-person approval, escalation paths, and how to interpret rollback signals.

decisions: Use three role archetypes (requester/approver/emergency-approver) to balance day-to-day speed and emergency override needs.
Audit logs stored in write-once S3 bucket with 12-month default retention and legal hold option for enterprise customers.
Approval gates will be opt-in per project with org-wide default set to 'required' for Dedicated and Private deployments.
Auto-approve policy allowed only for non-sensitive model families and must be explicitly whitelisted by security and product owners.
Initial rollout will support approvals for canary and promotion stages; A/B experiments will require approval before traffic rebalancing to new variant beyond 10%.
Expose an approvals API so infra-as-code (Terraform/CLI) can create pre-approved rollout templates for trusted automation.
